```{r setup, echo=FALSE}
library(AnimalTrackR)
```

AnimalTrackR has several python dependencies as YOLO is a python-based object detection framework. The vast majority of users will not need to interact directly with these dependencies. If you have any doubt, you go to the function documentation for `create_TrackR_env()`. This will install dependencies and handle environment creation correctly for almost all users.

If you have specific requirements based on your system, or other analysis pipelines, you can use this guide to create a custom environment that has the correct python version and packages to run AnimalTrackR. This guide assumes you have a working knowledge of Anaconda/Miniconda and managing python enviornments and packages.

## Environment

AnimalTrackR relies on a conda environment. It will not work with other types of python enviornment (e.g. virtual environments). Therefore, if you wish to create a custom environment you must first install conda. You can install the full release of [Anaconda](https://www.anaconda.com/docs/getting-started/anaconda/install), but we recommend the lightweight installation of [Miniconda](https://www.anaconda.com/docs/getting-started/miniconda/install). AnimalTrackR uses Miniconda by default.

## Python version

AnimalTrackR has been tested using python 3.11. Many of its dependencies will work with other python versions, but some issus have been reported with dependency conflicts in a number of commputer vision libraries, particularly pytorch, that may become problematic. Users can experiment with other python versions if they need to but we strongly reccomend staying with version 3.11.

## Python packages

AnimalTrackR uses these Python packages:

* **ultralytics**, the Python interface to YOLO ([documentation](https://docs.ultralytics.com/)), which in turn uses **torch** and **torchvision** (PyTorch)
* **opencv-python**, a widely used computer vision library used for reading and writing video and images ([details](https://pypi.org/project/opencv-python/))
* **numpy**, **pandas** and **matplotlib**, for handling and plotting data

`create_TrackR_env()` installs the exact versions that AnimalTrackR has been tested with. These are listed in a requirements file that comes with the package:

```{r requirements, eval=FALSE}
cat(readLines(system.file("python", "requirements.txt", package = "AnimalTrackR")), sep = "\n")
```

To create a custom environment with the same versions, install from this file with pip in your Python 3.11 conda environment:

```{bash custom-env, eval=FALSE}
pip install -r path/to/requirements.txt
```

where `path/to/requirements.txt` is the path returned by `system.file("python", "requirements.txt", package = "AnimalTrackR")`. Other versions will often work, but results may differ slightly and are not guaranteed. `check_TrackR_env()` lists any packages whose versions differ from the tested ones.

## Python packages for GPU support

If you have an NVIDIA GPU, PyTorch needs to be the build made for your CUDA version (find this by running `nvidia-smi` in a command prompt). The simplest way is to let AnimalTrackR do this for you, which installs the GPU build of the same tested PyTorch version:

```{r gpu, eval=FALSE}
configure_cuda(cuda.version = 13.1)  # use your own CUDA version
```

To do it by hand, install the tested `torch` and `torchvision` versions from PyTorch's package index for your CUDA version, for example for CUDA 13.0:

```{bash gpu-manual, eval=FALSE}
pip install torch==2.14.1 torchvision==0.29.1 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130
```

See [pytorch.org](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/) for the CUDA versions available.
